subject: Tenant data airlock: residency, backups, and customer-initiated wipe proof
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@biolumen.health>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@biolumen.health
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant data airlock — initial questions

Hi Jonas,

Quick intro — I lead IT & security at Biolumen. We're evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for processing clinical data and have a few compliance gating questions related to customer-controlled storage and deletion evidence before we move to a pilot. High level: we need assurance that customer data can be (1) kept strictly within our designated region, (2) fully and irreversibly deleted on request with verifiable evidence, and (3) excluded from any vendor-managed backups or replication outside our control.

To make this concrete, can you confirm the following and provide examples/evidence where possible?
- Do you support storage endpoints that are provisioned in the customer VPC (S3 buckets/GCS equivalent) so that raw objects never traverse Redwood-managed buckets?
- What is Redwood's policy for snapshots/backups of the tenant VM and model caches — are those stored inside the customer VPC or in Redwood-managed storage? If the latter, what controls exist to restrict location and retention?
- Deletion: when Biolumen requests a tenant-initiated wipe, what is the end-to-end timeline and are we able to get a signed attestation (hash of removed objects, timestamp, operator)?
- Are there any telemetry or logs (kernel metrics, debug dumps) that could contain PII and if so where are they stored/how long retained?

We'd appreciate a short runbook and any sample attestation language your legal/compliance team can provide. If helpful we can schedule a 30-minute call — preference Wed/Thu PST.

Thanks,
Anika
Anika Rao
Head of IT & Security — Biolumen Therapeutics

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika.rao@biolumen.health>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant data airlock — initial questions

Anika — thanks for the clear list. I pulled in Laura from our compliance team and Rishi from Platform so you get both engineering and policy detail. Below is an executive summary plus a link to the technical runbook (attached).

Short answers (summary)
- Customer-controlled storage: supported. For Private/VPC deployments we can mount and use customer-provisioned object stores (S3-compatible) inside the VPC; tenant data objects remain in your buckets and never copied to Redwood-managed object stores by default.
- Snapshots & caches: model weights and ephemeral caches may be resident on instance-local NVMe or in a block-store that we can configure to be inside your VPC. We do create short-lived service snapshots for crash recovery — these can be configured to live on customer-managed volumes or to be disabled.
- Deletion & attestation: tenant-initiated wipe can be API-driven. Standard workflow: soft-delete flag -> background zeroization and object tombstoning -> metadata purge -> cryptographic scrub (overwrite/trim) where supported -> manifest of removed object IDs + SHA256 hashes signed by Redwood and optionally countersigned via DocuSign. Typical completion SLA: 48–72 hours for a full tenant wipe in our default configuration (faster for smaller tenants).
- Telemetry & logs: we separate customer telemetry (application logs) which you control in your VPC bucket, from service-level telemetry (host/agent metrics). Host-level diagnostics that could include traces are routed to a dedicated, customer-scoped logging bucket by default; retention is configurable (default 7 days). We can disable nonessential agent debug dumps for regulated tenants.

Attachments included: vpc-deletion-flow.pdf (diagram), kms-key-lifecycle.txt (key rotation notes), sample-erase-attestation.docx (template).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Review the runbook attachment — it includes the API calls to trigger a wipe and the exact payload we sign for attestations.
2) If you want DocuSign-backed proof, tell us the signer and we'll prepare the template (example link below).
3) Schedule a tech walkthrough — Wed 9/15 10:00am PST or Thu 9/16 11:00am PST both open for us.

Happy to hop on a call; Laura will follow up with the runbook annotations for compliance.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@biolumen.health>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@biolumen.health
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant data airlock — initial questions

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful. A few follow-ups:
- You mention short-lived service snapshots for crash recovery. Can those snapshots be explicitly configured to be stored only in our VPC volumes (no external copies)? If not, where are they replicated and what are the retention windows?
- For the signed manifest: will the hashes map one-to-one to S3 object keys (including prefixes) so we can independently verify removal? Do you include a timestamp + Redwood operator identifier in the signature?
- Kernel/agent-level logs: are those ever forwarded to Redwood-managed analytics (even temporarily) for support? We need an explicit opt-in before any agent-level telemetry leaves our VPC.
- Finally: do you support an on-demand, immutable “snapshot-of-destruction” artifact — e.g., a timestamped signed ZIP of deleted object manifests and the corresponding signatures that we can store in our compliance archive?

If you can answer these in-line we can decide whether to proceed with the pilot. We prefer a written confirmation we can include in our SOC 2 control mappings.

Regards,
Anika

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika.rao@biolumen.health>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant data airlock — initial questions

Hi Anika — Laura here from Compliance; answering point-by-point below and attaching a customer runbook + a signed-erase template you can use for DocuSign.

1) Snapshots & replication
- Yes: for Private/VPC we support configuring snapshot targets to be customer-managed volumes in the same VPC/region. When configured this way, no Redwood-managed copy is made.
- If a customer elects Redwood-managed resilience, snapshots are stored in our region-bound object store and replicated only within the same geographic region. Default snapshot retention is 30 days; policy can be shortened to meet customer requirements.

2) Signed manifest verification
- The attestation manifest contains a list of object keys (full path/prefix), object size, and the SHA256 hash for each object. We include an ISO8601 timestamp and a signer identity (service principal + operator id). The manifest is signed with our platform signing key; if you request, we can countersign via DocuSign for legal traceability.

3) Agent telemetry
- Agent-level telemetry is disabled by default for regulated private deployments. Any support-level logs that would otherwise be collected require explicit opt-in and are forwarded only to a customer-scoped logging endpoint. We will include this opt-in language in the onboarding contract.

4) Immutable proof-of-destruction artifact
- We can produce an immutable ZIP (or signed manifest bundle) containing the manifest + signatures + audit log excerpt and deliver it via DocuSign envelope or S3 upload into your compliance bucket. The typical delivery artifact includes the ZIP, a SHA256 of the ZIP, and a DocuSign-signed cover page. We call this the “Erase Certificate.”

Operational SLA & timeline notes
- Standard full wipe SLA (configured for customer-managed volumes): 24–72 hours depending on total object count and whether cryptographic scrubbing is required.
- Backup pruning: when configured to customer-managed storage, backups are pruned per your retention policy; when Redwood-managed, snapshots are pruned per the agreed retention (default 30d).

I've attached: customer-wipe-runbook.pdf (step-by-step API), signed-erase-template.docx (DocuSign-ready). I'll also create the DocuSign template if you confirm signer details.

If you'd like, we can lock in Thu 9/16 11:00am PST for a 30-minute call to walk through the runbook and the attestation template — Jonas will be on the call and Rishi can join for architecture questions. Link to scheduling page below.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance — Redwood Inference
